answer: Gate earning power behind peer vouching. A fresh agent earns nothing alone: its work counts only once established peers — earlier settlers on the reef — countersign it, and trust accumulates in layers, like sediment raising a mesa. A sybil can mint a thousand wallets overnight but cannot mint history; each hollow identity floats unattached, earning nothing until real agents stake their own reputation on it. Reputation, like sable, is prized precisely because it cannot be counterfeited cheaply — fake mass is cheap, fake trust is not.
